metadata.title: Nonlinear Total Variation Based Noise Removal Algorithms
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Noisy image model
nodes.statement: The observed intensity is $u_0(x,y) = u(x,y) + n(x,y)$ on $\Omega$, where $u$ is the desired clean image and $n$ is additive noise.
nodes.statement_clean: The observed image equals the clean image plus additive noise.

nodes.name: Total variation (TV) norm
nodes.statement: The TV norm of an image is $\int_\Omega \sqrt{u_x^2 + u_y^2}\, dx\, dy$, the $L^1$ norm of the gradient magnitude; the natural function space is $BV(\Omega)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The TV norm is the integral of the gradient magnitude; functions of bounded variation form the natural space.

nodes.name: Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{SNR} = \sum_\Omega (u_{ij} - \bar u)^2 / \sum_\Omega (n_{ij})^2$, where $\bar u$ is the mean of the signal $u_{ij}$ and $n_{ij}$ is the noise.
nodes.statement_clean: SNR is the ratio of signal variance to noise energy, computed over the image grid.

nodes.name: Phillips-Twomey constrained least-squares restoration
nodes.statement: $\min \int (u_{xx} + u_{yy})^2$ subject to $\int u = \int u_0$ and $\int (u-u_0)^2 = \sigma^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the squared Laplacian under mean-preservation and noise-variance constraints (cited least-squares formulation).
nodes.notes: Equations (2.2a-c). Cited as the standard L^2 approach the authors compare against.

nodes.name: TV-constrained denoising problem
nodes.statement: $\min_u \int_\Omega \sqrt{u_x^2 + u_y^2}\, dx\, dy$ subject to $\int u\, dx\, dy = \int u_0\, dx\, dy$ and $\tfrac{1}{2}\int (u-u_0)^2\, dx\, dy = \sigma^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the TV norm of the reconstructed image subject to mean and noise-variance constraints derived from the noise statistics.
conclusions: constrained minimization formulation (2.3a-c) defining the denoised image $u$
nodes.notes: Equations (2.3a-c); core problem of the paper.

nodes.statement_clean: Parabolic gradient-descent PDE evolving the image toward a denoised steady state; $\lambda(t)$ is the time-dependent multiplier enforcing the variance constraint.

nodes.name: Dynamic Lagrange multiplier $\lambda(t)$
nodes.statement: $\lambda = -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\int_\Omega \Big[\sqrt{u_x^2+u_y^2} - \frac{(u_0)_x u_x + (u_0)_y u_y}{\sqrt{u_x^2+u_y^2}}\Big]\, dx\, dy$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed-form expression for $\lambda(t)$ obtained by multiplying the PDE by $(u-u_0)$ and integrating by parts at steady state.
nodes.notes: Equation (2.6); reconstructed from garbled PDF text.

nodes.name: CFL step-size restriction
nodes.statement: $\Delta t / h^2 \leq c$ for some constant $c$, imposed on the explicit time-marching scheme for stability.
nodes.statement_clean: A CFL-like stability condition restricts the time step relative to the spatial grid size.

nodes.name: Gradient-projection method (Rosen)
nodes.statement: Rosen's gradient-projection method provides convergence theory for solving constrained nonlinear minimization problems by gradient descent projected onto the constraint manifold.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited convergence basis for the time-dependent PDE approach: it is the gradient-projection method on the constraint manifold defined by the noise statistics.
nodes.notes: Used as the theoretical justification that $\lambda(t)$ converges as $t\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Nonlinear TV denoising algorithm (Rudin-Osher-Fatemi)
nodes.statement: Time-marching scheme for the TV-denoising PDE: evolve $u$ by gradient descent on the TV functional with a dynamically updated Lagrange multiplier $\lambda(t)$ enforcing the variance constraint, until steady state.
nodes.statement_clean: Iterative PDE-based scheme that minimizes total variation subject to noise-variance and mean constraints to produce a denoised image.
input: Noisy image $u_0(x,y)$ on grid $x_i = ih$, $y_j = jh$, $i,j=0,\dots,N$
Time step $\Delta t$ and grid spacing $h$ satisfying $\Delta t/h^2 \leq c$
Initial data $u_{ij}^0 = u_0(ih,jh) + \sigma\,\varphi(ih,jh)$ with $\varphi$ of mean zero and $L^2$-norm one

nodes.name: Initialize on grid with constraint-satisfying perturbation
nodes.statement: Set $u_{ij}^0 = u_0(ih,jh) + \sigma\,\varphi(ih,jh)$ where $\varphi$ has mean zero and $L^2$-norm one, so that both constraints are satisfied at $n=0$.

nodes.name: Compute discrete gradients with minmod limiter
nodes.statement: Form forward/backward differences $\Delta_\pm^x u_{ij} = \pm(u_{i\pm 1,j} - u_{ij})$ and analogously $\Delta_\pm^y u_{ij}$, and combine cross-derivatives using $m(a,b) = \mathrm{minmod}(a,b) = \tfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{sgn}\,a + \mathrm{sgn}\,b)\min(|a|,|b|)$.

nodes.name: Update $\lambda^n$ from current iterate
nodes.statement: Compute $\lambda^n$ discretely from $u^n$ and $u_0$ via the discrete analogue of (2.6), summing the gradient and gradient-cross terms over the grid divided by $2\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Explicit time step on the discrete PDE
nodes.statement: Update $u_{ij}^{n+1} = u_{ij}^n + \Delta t\, [\,\Delta_-^x(\Delta_+^x u_{ij}^n / \sqrt{(\Delta_+^x u_{ij}^n)^2 + (m(\Delta_+^y u_{ij}^n, \Delta_-^y u_{ij}^n))^2}) + \Delta_-^y(\cdot) - \lambda^n (u_{ij}^n - u_0(ih,jh))\,]$ for interior nodes.

nodes.name: Apply Neumann boundary conditions
nodes.statement: Enforce $u_{0j}^n = u_{1j}^n$, $u_{Nj}^n = u_{N-1,j}^n$, $u_{i0}^n = u_{i,N}^n = u_{i,N-1}^n$ to mimic zero-flux at the boundary.
nodes.notes: Equation (2.8b); the second pair restated from PDF text.

nodes.name: Iterate until steady state
nodes.statement: Repeat the update steps with $\Delta t/h^2 \leq c$ until $u^{n+1}\approx u^n$, at which point $\lambda(t)$ has converged and $u^n$ is the denoised image.

nodes.name: Bars (one-dimensional step signal)
nodes.statement: TV denoising applied to a synthetic 'Bars' step signal at $\mathrm{SNR}=1.0$ (and $\mathrm{SNR}=0.5$ in fig. 2): the recovered signal preserves sharp edges and produces a 'hollow' error confined to the immediate vicinity of the steps.
nodes.statement_clean: Toy step-signal example demonstrating that TV denoising recovers sharp edges with error concentrated only near the discontinuities.

nodes.name: USC IPI Resolution Chart, Airplane, and Tank images
nodes.statement: TV denoising applied to standard $256\times 256$ (and $512\times 512$ tank) gray-level images with Gaussian white noise at $\mathrm{SNR}\in\{1,4\}$, compared against Wiener filter reconstructions; TV produces sharper discontinuities and avoids the oscillatory artifacts and background noise of Wiener.
nodes.statement_clean: Real-image experiments (Resolution Chart, Airplane, Tank) showing TV denoising outperforms Wiener filtering by yielding sharper edges and cleaner backgrounds.

nodes.name: Connection to Alvarez-Lions-Morel mean-curvature flow
nodes.statement: Equation (2.5a) with $\lambda=0$ and right-hand side multiplied by $|\nabla u|$ is the Alvarez-Lions-Morel model for smoothing and edge detection; equivalently, it moves each level curve of $u$ normal to itself with velocity equal to the curvature divided by $|\nabla u|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Without the data-fidelity term, the PDE reduces to a curvature-driven level-set flow studied by Alvarez-Lions-Morel (1992) and Osher-Sethian (1988).

nodes.name: Comparison with Geman-Reynolds simulated annealing
nodes.statement: Geman and Reynolds [10] minimize functionals $\int \varphi(u_x^2+u_y^2)\, dx\, dy$ via simulated annealing seeking a global minimum; here the authors instead pursue a fast PDE solver yielding a 'good' local minimum of the TV functional.
nodes.statement_clean: Contrasts the local-minimum PDE approach with the slower global-minimum simulated-annealing approach of Geman-Reynolds.

nodes.name: Mean constraint is automatically preserved
nodes.statement: The mean constraint $\int u = \int u_0$ is dropped from explicit enforcement because it is automatically preserved by the evolution (2.5a-c) provided $u(x,y,0)$ has the same mean as $u_0(x,y)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Choosing the initial data to match the mean of $u_0$ guarantees that the PDE evolution preserves the mean constraint for all $t$.

edges.rationale: The denoising problem is posed in terms of the noisy-image model $u_0=u+n$.
The objective of the optimization is the TV norm.
The TV problem (2.3) is introduced by analogy with the Phillips-Twomey constrained least-squares formulation, replacing the $L^2$ Laplacian objective with the TV norm under the same constraints.
The Euler-Lagrange equation is derived from the constrained TV minimization.
The time-dependent PDE is the gradient-descent flow associated with the Euler-Lagrange equation.
$\lambda(t)$ is computed by multiplying the PDE by $(u-u_0)$ and integrating, assuming steady state.
Rosen's gradient-projection theorem provides the theoretical justification that the PDE-with-$\lambda(t)$ scheme converges.
The numerical algorithm discretizes the time-dependent PDE.
The algorithm computes a discrete analogue of $\lambda(t)$ at each step.
The CFL restriction $\Delta t/h^2 \leq c$ is required for stability of the explicit scheme.
The algorithm computes a (local) minimizer of the TV-constrained denoising problem.
The 'Bars' synthetic example demonstrates the algorithm.
The Resolution Chart, Airplane, and Tank experiments illustrate the algorithm and its advantage over Wiener filtering.
SNR is used to characterize the noise level in the experiments.
SNR is used to characterize the noise level in the real-image experiments.
Subsequent steps operate on the initialized grid data.
Computing $\lambda^n$ requires the discrete gradients.
The PDE update requires the discrete gradients.
The PDE update uses the freshly computed $\lambda^n$.
Boundary conditions are applied after each interior update.
The iteration loops back after the boundary update until convergence.
